title: How to (Accidentally) Survive Baku Wedding Season. Tip #1
body: Count the invitations. If there are three this month it's a normal season. If there are eight, somebody in the family has reached the age where all the cousins go at once, and there is nothing anyone can do. Each one is a şadlıq sarayı, five hundred guests minimum, and he knows four of them. It's a sealed deal if he has been to a wedding where he could not identify the groom until the third hour.
caption:
Tip #1 😭 toy season is a full-time job.

title: How to (Accidentally) Survive Baku Wedding Season. Tip #2
body: Watch the outfit maths. The same suit cannot appear at two weddings where the photo sets overlap, and everybody has quietly mapped which cousins were at which. The women's side of this calculation is a full-time intelligence operation with a group chat. It's a sealed deal if somebody has changed an outfit at the last minute because of who else was confirmed attending.
caption:
Tip #2 😭 toy season is a full-time job.

title: How to (Accidentally) Survive Baku Wedding Season. Tip #3
body: Ask about the singer, because the singer is the budget. Everyone knows the tiers, everyone knows roughly what the top ones cost, and the choice tells the whole room what the family spent. When the good one arrives the average age on the dance floor drops by twenty years instantly. It's a sealed deal if a relative has said the singer's fee out loud, at the table, to strangers.
caption:
Tip #3 😭 toy season is a full-time job.

title: How to (Accidentally) Survive Baku Wedding Season. Tip #4
body: Watch the money moment. Pinning, handing, the envelope, whichever the family does, and everyone is counting without appearing to count. There is one uncle who does it loudly and one who does it in a way nobody sees. Both are making a statement. It's a sealed deal if somebody has been discussed for a week afterwards over the amount.
caption:
Tip #4 😭 toy season is a full-time job.

title: How to (Accidentally) Survive Baku Wedding Season. Tip #5
body: Ask how many events there actually are, because outsiders think a wedding is a day. Elçilik, nişan, xınayaxdı, then the toy, and each one has its own guest list, its own outfits, its own arguments. By the actual wedding everyone has been at this for months and is running on nothing. It's a sealed deal if somebody has cried over a seating chart and it was not the bride.
caption:
Tip #5 😭 toy season is a full-time job.

title: How to (Accidentally) Survive Baku Wedding Season. Tip #6
body: Watch the qayınana dynamic, because the whole room is watching it and pretending not to. Every conversation in the family for six months has been about this and it will be discussed for years afterwards, in detail, from both sides. It's a sealed deal if two women are being extremely polite to each other in a way that everyone present can read perfectly.
caption:
Tip #6 😭 toy season is a full-time job.

title: How to (Accidentally) Survive Baku Wedding Season. Tip #7
body: Ask what happens at the end. The plov arrives, that's the signal, and the room begins the long slow business of leaving, which takes ninety minutes. Somebody's grandmother is still dancing. Somebody's father is arguing about who is driving whom. It's a sealed deal if he has ever left a wedding at 1am and gone straight to a chai place with four cousins to talk about the wedding.
caption:
Tip #7 😭 toy season is a full-time job.
